long_biography.plain_text:
An integrative-health conference redirected Terri DeNeui's path from acute hospital care to prevention. She opened a clinic while still working hospital shifts and sustained both roles for five years. She later made hormone therapy the subject of her doctoral research at the University of Texas at Arlington. The experience shaped an approach that joined clinical practice, practitioner instruction and evidence translation.

Her reach later extended beyond patient care. Through national courses, conference teaching and peer-reviewed writing, DeNeui trained other clinicians in functional and regenerative medicine. She also wrote a consumer guide to hormone health and began a weekly educational podcast. Appearances before federal pharmacy advisers and participation in professional policy groups added a public-policy dimension to a career rooted in bedside nursing and preventive care.
